from.place: Comparator challenge theorem WeilConjectures.zetaSeries_rational (lean/Comparator/Weil/Challenge.lean): rationality of the zeta series of any finite-type quasi-compact scheme over a finite field

title: WeilConjectures.zetaSeries_rational (Dwork rationality)
statement: Let k be a finite field and f:X->Spec k a morphism of schemes that is locally of finite type and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For a finite field k with q=#k elements, a scheme X and a morphism f:X->Spec k, the zeta series Z(X,t)=f.zetaSeries in Q[[t]] [def-weil-point-counts-zeta] is Z(X,t)=exp(sum_{n>=1} N_n t^n/n), substituted into the formal exponential series, where N_n=f.pointCount n is the number of k-morphisms Spec F_{q^n} -> X (morphisms g with g followed by f equal to the map induced by k -> F_{q^n}), F_{q^n} being the model FiniteField.galoisExtension k n = the splitting field over k of X^{q^n}-X, and N_n=0 (junk value) if this set is infinite. A polynomial with integer coefficients is viewed in Q[[t]] through its coefficientwise image in Q[t] [def-weil-coefficientwise-extension, def-weil-polynomial-as-power-series]. Then there are polynomials P,Q in Z[t] [def-weil-polynomial-ring] with constant coefficient Q(0)=1 [def-weil-polynomial-coefficient] such that Z(X,t)*Q = P in Q[[t]] [def-weil-formal-power-series]. No smoothness, properness or separatedness is assumed.
